items.title: UN Security Council condemns 'escalatory' Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia
items.summary: UN Security Council condemns 'escalatory' Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia The UN Security Council has condemned the "escalatory" attacks by Iran-backed Houthis on Saudi Arabia, including "reckless strikes" on Riyadh's airport. The Saudi capital's international airport has been targeted by strikes 20 times since the beginning of the month, with an attack last weekend killing 13 people and wounding more than 300. In a joint statement shared by the Security Council's president, Greece's Evangelos Sekeris, the 15-member UN body also condemned "continued Houthi attacks and threats against commercial shipping in the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab (Strait)". The statement also "affirmed the inherent right of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia of self-defence in accordance with international law."

items.title: Rubio says Russia sanctions pause to 'analyse' impact on global economy
items.summary: Rubio says Russia sanctions pause to 'analyse' impact on global economy US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Saturday that President Donald Trump's waiver of sweeping sanctions and tariffs on Russia would be a 60-day pause to "analyse" their impact on the global economy and "even to the US economy". Rubio said the economic restrictions involved a number of countries, not just Russia. He said various conflicts were impacting global energy prices, including the US war on Iran and attacks on Saudi Arabia by Yemen's Houthis. items.summary: Iran's IRGC navy says oil tanker hits mine, catches fire in Strait of Hormuz An oil tanker caught fire and exploded after striking a naval mine in the southern part of the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) navy said on Sunday, according to Iranian media. The vessel violated Iran-imposed “regulations” by switching off its navigation system while transiting the waterway, the IRGC said. “An illicit oil tanker exploded and caught fire in its engine room after hitting a naval mine in the southern Strait of Hormuz,” the Fars news agency quoted the IRGC as saying. “If ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz and the Persian Gulf switch off their navigation and identification systems, they will be dealt with severely and decisively.”

items.summary: Two Indian nationals missing after drone attack on tanker off Oman's coast A drone attack on a vessel off the coast of Oman left two Indian nations missing, a senior Indian official said on Sunday. Meanwhile, nine others were rescued, as search and rescue operations by the local coast guard begin. "On Oct 11, tanker MT PETRO DOLPHIN, carrying 11 Indian seafarers, was subjected to a drone attack at Sohar Anchorage," Indian Shipping Minister Sarbananda Sonowal said in a post on X. "While nine of our Indian crew members have been successfully rescued and are safe, two Indian nationals currently remain missing." Sonowal added that India is "continuously coordinating with all relevant authorities to fully support the ongoing rescue efforts and ensure every possible action is taken to safely locate our missing personnel". Since the war on Iran began in late February, at least 16 Indian seafarers have been killed.

In an interview on the sidelines of the IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok, Muhammad Aurangzeb told AFP said the South Asian country had procured enough energy supplies to last through November, and was now planning for the winter months, when household needs typically spike. "The first-order impact has been negotiated well by Pakistan," he said. "We've had no shortage, no queues at the gas stations, and no law and order situation, which at times we have seen in some of the countries." He added that unless the government saw "an absolute dire need", it would not be procuring spot cargoes on the LNG front, which tend to be far more expensive than previously contracted shipments. The navy described the tanker as "violating", saying it had switched off its tracking systems. It gave no indication of what had caused the fire. The navy said uncoordinated movements along routes and in prohibited areas created insecurity and posed significant risks to other vessels. Reporting by Reuters

It was not immediately clear what caused the fire or who was responsible.

items.summary: Iran says US response falls short of conditions for deal Tehran continues to demand changes to Washington’s response before agreeing to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and resume talks, according to Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei. “The US has agreed to some of Iran’s seven conditions, but we consider its response inadequate,” the Supreme National Security Council secretary wrote on X. “Iranian diplomacy has changed and there will be no return to the status quo ante,” he added. Iran’s demands include lifting the US naval blockade and removing restrictions on its oil exports. Tehran has offered to restore passage through the strait and restart negotiations once Washington meets its conditions. Rezaei previously ruled out opening the waterway to the US or beginning talks before Washington satisfies those demands. The U.S. has agreed to some of Iran’s seven conditions, but we consider its response INADEQUATE. items.title: Iran’s security chief calls US response to deal conditions ‘inadequate’
items.summary: Iran’s security chief calls US response to deal conditions ‘inadequate’ Washington must clarify its position before talks on a possible agreement can advance, Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei says. “The Americans have now responded to us. In their response, they have accepted some of our conditions, while others remain unclear,” the Supreme National Security Council secretary told the semi-official Tasnim news agency. Rezaei described the US response as “inadequate”. “We are no longer in the process of responding to the Americans,” he said. “They must clarify the issues that remain unclear to us,” he added. The exchange follows President Donald Trump’s rejection late last month of an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days. US Vice President JD Vance subsequently demanded a “meaningful” reduction in Iran’s uranium enrichment capacity as a condition for an agreement.

clusters.headline: US seeks 'verifiable commitment' Iran won't rebuild nuclear programme, Vance says

items.title: US seeks 'verifiable commitment' Iran won't rebuild nuclear programme, Vance says
items.summary: US seeks 'verifiable commitment' Iran won't rebuild nuclear programme, Vance says US Vice President JD Vance said Washington was focused on securing Iran’s “long-term” and “verifiable commitment” not to rebuild its nuclear programme, while claiming the US had “in some ways decisively won” the war against Iran and destroyed its nuclear programme. Speaking at a town hall hosted by CBS News, Vance said the focus was on preventing Iran from rebuilding its nuclear capabilities in the years ahead. “Not over the administration of Donald Trump… but five years from now, could the Iranians rebuild that nuclear arsenal? items.summary: Iran’s attacks on Hormuz shipping 'unsuccessful', Centcom says The US military says the “vast majority” of Iran’s attempted attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz have failed, and that the waterway remains open. On Saturday, US Central Command spokesperson Tim Hawkins told Fox News that about 97 percent of vessels trying to cross the strait had done so without being struck, many of them with US military protection. “What the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps of Iran is doing is unjustified and it’s also unsuccessful because they are not achieving their objective of closing the Strait of Hormuz,” Hawkins said.

items.title: Hormuz controlled by US and allies, not Iran: Centcom chief
items.summary: Hormuz controlled by US and allies, not Iran: Centcom chief The Strait of Hormuz "is controlled by the United States and our regional partners, not Iran ", the head of US Central Command (Centcom) has said. In a video statement, Centcom commander Brad Cooper said the US blockade of Iranian ports had imposed "a devastating cost" on the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). He said it had completely halted Iran's maritime exports and imports, "with the exception of humanitarian assistance we have allowed in". Cooper said the US had "prevented Iran from exporting at least 25 billion dollars worth of crude oil" and had "significantly degraded Iran's ability to project power far beyond its borders". He added that US forces had helped Gulf allies ship more than 100 million barrels of crude through the strait in the past week, with around 400 merchant vessels passing through. In total, the US had helped regional partners move 1.3 billion barrels through Hormuz in recent months, he said.

items.summary: US weighs lifting sanctions on Iran's 'shadow fleet' to address surging costs The US is considering lifting sanctions on “shadow fleet” tankers tied to Russia and Iran to address soaring diesel prices ahead of midterm elections, according to multiple reports and a senior US official. US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said in a video address to an energy forum in Riyadh this week that the Trump administration was discussing easing sanctions on shadow fleet vessels to address record freight rates that have driven up costs of shipping American energy abroad, Energy Aspects, a research group, said. The Financial Times reported on Thursday that the US could allow the sale of blacklisted vessels to non-sanctioned operators and lift sanctions, allowing them to operate without restrictions. Reuters reported the US could allow “legal oil" to flow on previously sanctioned vessels, effectively allowing sanctioned ships to carry crude or petroleum products not sanctioned by the US. clusters.headline: La poesía no ha muerto

items.title: La poesía no ha muerto
items.summary: Dice Andrés Trapiello que la poesía no ha muerto, esto es que vive, pero no así el mundo que la necesitaba. Lo dice, a su manera, para celebrar un aniversario de la editorial La Veleta, que el escritor fundó hace ahora cien libros de poemas, después de otras aventuras editoriales, como Trieste. Y lo celebra con la publicación de las traducciones de Emily Dickinson que debemos a Carlos Pujol, lector y traductor y persona inmejorable. Que el mundo haya necesitado la poesía alguna vez es una interesante hipótesis que muchos hechos podrían desmentir. But maybe we should just be grateful he refrained from rubbishing the South African human rights activist Navi Pillay, who picked up the award , and shelved his plans to livestream the execution of the Norwegian prize committee. items.title: Delegations from over ten countries walk out of Israeli president's CICA summit speech
items.summary: Delegations from over ten countries walk out of Israeli president's CICA summit speech Representatives from more than 10 countries, including Turkey, walked out of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence Building Measures in Asia (CICA) summit in Azerbaijan as Israeli President Isaac Herzog began his speech on Thursday. Iran’s deputy legal affairs minister called for Israel to be expelled from CICA following Herzog's speech in Baku. Kazem Gharibabadi was quoted as saying by Iran's IRIB news that “sustainable security” in Asia was not achieved through “threats and pressure, but through mutual respect, trust-building and equal cooperation among independent states”. “If the international community does not stop America and Israel today, their aggression will spread to all independent countries. items.title: Chinese refiners rush to buy Middle East crude as stocks fall, Kpler says
items.summary: Chinese refiners rush to buy Middle East crude as stocks fall, Kpler says Chinese refiners are stepping up purchases of Middle Eastern crude as record inventory drawdowns and a recovery in refinery activity boost demand for prompt cargoes, according to analytics firm Kpler. Chinese buyers have secured at least 80 million barrels of Saudi crude since mid-September, Kpler said on X. China’s onshore crude inventories fell by about 1.6 million barrels per day in September, the fastest pace on record. Refinery throughput is projected to reach 14.2 million barrels per day by December, adding to pressure on refiners to rebuild stocks. At the same time, Chinese refiners need to replace roughly 1 million barrels per day of Iranian supply, with the US blockade still in place, according to Kpler. Stronger Chinese demand could limit further weakness in Dubai crude pricing, particularly as escalating regional tensions continue to threaten supply flows.

Het kleine containerschip GFS Pride dat onder Singaporese vlag voer, zonk toen het gisteren tijdens de doorvaart door de zeestraat werd geraakt. Op het schip brak brand uit, meldt de maritieme dienst van Singapore. Niemand raakte gewond, de 21 bemanningsleden zijn geëvacueerd. Het tweede schip Cape Dao, dat onder de vlag van Antigua en Barbuda voer, zonk in de buurt van Oman. Dat schip werd al op 23 september door een projectiel geraakt. Een bemanningslid kwam toen om het leven. De andere opvarenden werden volgens maritieme bronnen direct na de inslag geëvacueerd. As the issue becomes harder to avoid, Republican candidates in Iowa and Maine have signaled a break with President Donald Trump and his war. Now, they are being pressed on something tougher than whether they want the conflict over: what they would actually do to end it. Iowa is one of the typically red states now playing host to a razor-close race in 2026. The war’s economic fallout has been a particularly potent political issue in Iowa, perhaps because the state’s gas prices have jumped 69% — tied for the nation’s largest increase , according to AAA data from late August — and because it is among the country’s most farming-dependent states. The MoU is a 14-point interim peace agreement signed electronically on 17-18 June between the United States and Iran, with Pakistan acting as the primary mediator. Zardari called for differences to be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy, emphasising the importance of safe maritime navigation through the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea, according to a statement from his office. His remarks came during a meeting with Russian Interior Minister Vladimir Kolokoltsev in Islamabad. Zardari warned that the conflict posed serious challenges to regional stability, global energy security, trade and supply chains, stressing the need to respect the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all states. Kolokoltsev is on a four-day official visit to Pakistan, the first by a Russian interior minister to the South Asian country.

The next most intense period of attacks was during the first two weeks of March, when 13 ships were hit, the newspaper said, citing data from naval agency UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO), which monitors marine security in the region. Shipowners are reconsider carrying cargoes in the region, the report said. Six vessels were attacked on Sunday alone, making it the deadliest day of attacks on shipping near the strait since the start of the conflict, FT calculated. It added that oil shipments through Hormuz fell to just 2.9 million barrels on 11 October, the lowest daily volume this month, according to Kpler.

Dat zeggen de Saudische burgerluchtvaartautoriteiten. Het is daarmee de dodelijkste aanval in een Golfstaat sinds het begin van de oorlog tussen de VS en Israël met Iran in februari. The New York Times meldt dat de Houthi-rebellen via een hoge functionaris de verantwoordelijkheid hebben opgeëist van de aanval. Volgens hem was de aanval een vergelding voor Saudische luchtaanvallen op Jemen, waaronder aanvallen op civiele infrastructuur. De luchthaven King Khalid is de een na grootste van Saudi-Arabië, na die in Jeddah. De schade aan de terminal wordt nu in kaart gebracht. Er zijn vrijwel geen foto's of videobeelden beschikbaar van het vliegveld na de inslagen. Het vliegverkeer is stilgelegd. Deze geverifieerde beelden zijn er wel: Onder de doden zijn volgens de Saudische autoriteiten vier mensen uit Saudi-Arabië. Twee anderen zijn afkomstig uit Bangladesh. De overige slachtoffers komen uit de VS, Egypte, Jordanië, Syrië, Sudan en de Palestijns

items.title: Gewonden bij aanval op luchthaven in Saudische hoofdstad Riyad, vliegverkeer ligt stil
items.summary: Bij aanvallen op de internationale luchthaven in de Saudische hoofdstad Riyad is een onbekend aantal gewonden gevallen. Twee regionale functionarissen zeggen dat het vliegveld is ontruimd nadat een raket een passagiersterminal had geraakt. Volgens getuigen reden ambulances met spoed naar de luchthaven. Al het vliegverkeer van en naar King Khalid International Airport is stilgelegd. Een bron in een plaatselijk ziekenhuis vertelde aan persbureau AFP dat bij de aanval tientallen gewonden zijn gevallen. Hij zag hoe gate 401 van de binnenlandse terminal werd getroffen. "Ik zag met mijn eigen ogen de gewonden. Iedereen rende weg." Uit gegevens van Flightaware blijkt dat de afgelopen 24 uur minstens 225 vluchten op King Khalid International Airport zijn geannuleerd, na de eerdere aanvallen op de luchthaven deze week. De luchthaven roept reizigers op contact op te nemen met hun luchtvaartmaatschappij en de status van hun vlucht te controleren voordat ze naar de luchthaven komen. items.title: Iran’s security chief accuses Trump administration of oil smuggling near Oman
items.summary: Iran’s security chief accuses Trump administration of oil smuggling near Oman Mohsen Rezaei has accused the Trump administration of recruiting “thugs” to smuggle oil through coastal waters off Oman. Iran’s Supreme National Security Council secretary said the UAE military and the commander of US Central Command also participate in the operation, according to state-linked news agency ISNA. Trump “claims every day that the Strait of Hormuz is open, but in response I say: ‘You are smuggling, but the strait is under Iranian control and we manage it,'” Rezaei said. He said the operation relies on a handful of “small vessels to transfer oil to larger tankers”, adding that Iran attacks them “every night”.

items.title: Iran security chief accuses Trump of ‘smuggling’ oil through Hormuz
items.summary: Iran security chief accuses Trump of ‘smuggling’ oil through Hormuz Iran’s security chief claimed on Sunday that US President Donald Trump's adminitation hired “thugs” in the coastal waters of Oman to smuggle oil through the Iranian blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. Trump “claims every day that the Strait of Hormuz is open, but in response I say: ‘You are smuggling, but the strait is under Iranian control and we manage it,'” Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei was quoted as saying by Iran's ISNA news agency. Rezaei said that the smuggling operation involves the UAE military and the commander of US Central Command (Centcom) using a handful of “small vessels to transfer oil to larger tankers” and that Iran targets them “every night”.

items.title: Saudi-Arabië zal 'stevig terugslaan' na Houthi-aanval op luchthaven Riyad

Saudi-Arabië belooft stevig terug te slaan, terwijl er nu al hard wordt gevochten tussen de Houthi's en de door Saudi-Arabië gesteunde regeringstroepen in Jemen. Directeur Dania Thafer van onderzoeksinstituut Gulf International Forum in Washington verwacht dat de Saudi's "behoorlijk hard" zullen terugslaan. Tegen nieuwssite Al Jazeera zegt ze: "Ik denk nog steeds dat de Saudi's de-escalatie willen. Ze willen geen langdurige escalatie. Maar de Houthi's maken het erg moeilijk, omdat ze niet alleen een bedreiging vormen voor de nationale veiligheid van Saudi-Arabië, maar ook voor de internationale maritieme veiligheid." Mogelijk is een eerste militaire reactie al begonnen. Houthi-milities melden een Saudische aanval op de door hen gecontroleerde luchthaven van Sanaa. items.summary: Iranian nuclear technology safe from US attacks, says atomic energy chief The head of Iran's atomic energy agency said on Sunday that the country's nuclear technology is safe from external disruption and cannot be halted by threats, pressure or attacks. Mohammad Eslami, the chief of the Atomic Energy Organisation of Iran (AEOI), said Iran's nuclear advances are a national achievement and were a testament to the dedication of Iranian scientists. “Overt threats by US officials to use tactical weapons against Iran’s nuclear facilities - delivered right from the United Nations podium - and talk of destroying Iran’s ancient civilisation, reveal helplessness in the face of a pioneering nation that has historically been the cradle of science, knowledge and technology,” Eslami was quoted as saying by Iran’s semi-official Tasnim news agency, adding that the nation will not surrender to excessive demands. US President Donald Trump has repeatedly affirmed Washington's intention to wipe out Iran's nuclear capabilities and ensure that the country will never be able to develop the technology.

items.summary: Israeli politician says assassinating Ali Khamenei was a ‘mistake’ The leader of Israel’s Democrats party on Saturday has called the assassination of Iranian Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei a “mistake”. “I think, unequivocally, the elimination of Khamenei, the father, was a mistake - not because he didn’t deserve to die, only because it doesn’t serve the interests of the State of Israel,” Yair Golan said. He also added that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s goal of toppling the Iranian government was “unrealistic”. Khamenei was assassinated at the beginning of the US-Israel war and has been succeeded by his son, Mojtaba. The new supreme leader is believed to be far less risk-averse than his father, who had issued a fatwa in 2003 banning nuclear weapons in Iran. clusters.headline: Increased vessel attacks drive Hormuz oil exports 'sharply lower', report says

items.title: Increased vessel attacks drive Hormuz oil exports 'sharply lower', report says
items.summary: Increased vessel attacks drive Hormuz oil exports 'sharply lower', report says Hormuz oil exports were “sharply lower,” falling to a seven-day average of 9.9 million barrels per day as of October 7, 42 percent below prewar levels and down from about 15.5 million in September, according to Kpler data cited by the Financial Times. Kpler said that flows had recovered to prewar levels in September but "intensified attacks on vessels" had driven exports "sharply lower" this week. Energy analyst Rory Johnston also said that the latest estimate puts Hormuz seven-day average oil flow peaking at 16.2 mbpd on September 24. "Then Iran really picked up its shipping attacks and that flow unsurprisingly pulled back by 3-4 mbpd," he wrote on X. "Now seeing flow at 12-13 mbpd over the past two weeks."

items.title: Iran's IRGC navy says oil tanker hits mine, catches fire in Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: Iran's IRGC navy says oil tanker hits mine, catches fire in Strait of Hormuz An oil tanker caught fire and exploded after striking a naval mine in the southern part of the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) navy said on Sunday, according to Iranian media. The vessel violated Iran-imposed “regulations” by switching off its navigation system while transiting the waterway, the IRGC said. “An illicit oil tanker exploded and caught fire in its engine room after hitting a naval mine in the southern Strait of Hormuz,” the Fars news agency quoted the IRGC as saying. “If ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz and the Persian Gulf switch off their navigation and identification systems, they will be dealt with severely and decisively.”

Reuters reported the US could allow “legal oil" to flow on previously sanctioned vessels, effectively allowing sanctioned ships to carry crude or petroleum products not sanctioned by the US. items.title: Hormuz controlled by US and allies, not Iran: Centcom chief
items.summary: Hormuz controlled by US and allies, not Iran: Centcom chief The Strait of Hormuz "is controlled by the United States and our regional partners, not Iran ", the head of US Central Command (Centcom) has said. In a video statement, Centcom commander Brad Cooper said the US blockade of Iranian ports had imposed "a devastating cost" on the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). He said it had completely halted Iran's maritime exports and imports, "with the exception of humanitarian assistance we have allowed in". Cooper said the US had "prevented Iran from exporting at least 25 billion dollars worth of crude oil" and had "significantly degraded Iran's ability to project power far beyond its borders". He added that US forces had helped Gulf allies ship more than 100 million barrels of crude through the strait in the past week, with around 400 merchant vessels passing through. In total, the US had helped regional partners move 1.3 billion barrels through Hormuz in recent months, he said.

items.title: La poesía no ha muerto
items.summary: Dice Andrés Trapiello que la poesía no ha muerto, esto es que vive, pero no así el mundo que la necesitaba. Lo dice, a su manera, para celebrar un aniversario de la editorial La Veleta, que el escritor fundó hace ahora cien libros de poemas, después de otras aventuras editoriales, como Trieste. Y lo celebra con la publicación de las traducciones de Emily Dickinson que debemos a Carlos Pujol, lector y traductor y persona inmejorable. Que el mundo haya necesitado la poesía alguna vez es una interesante hipótesis que muchos hechos podrían desmentir. O muchos versos: la flor que el arado destroza en el poema de Catulo, las cuatro personas para las que escribía Pound (¡oh mundo, lo siento por ti!), la tumba en el aire que excavan los judíos de la ‘Fuga de la muerte’ de Celan, o el combatiente ejecutado ante los ojos de René Char, caído como una hoja que una ráfaga de viento arrastraría... O la misma ausencia que Omar Jayyam mostró a la Luna hace mil años desde un huerto en el Jorasán iraní: ‘Cuantas y cuantas veces volverás a buscarme en el mismo jardín y todo será inútil’. Significantly, the Iran war has surpassed immigration and crime, two issues on which President Donald Trump performed particularly well in 2024, among voters’ top concerns. In the 2024 campaign, pre - and post -election polling showed those issues as ranking higher as a priority for voters than foreign policy. items.title: UN Security Council condemns 'escalatory' Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia
items.summary: UN Security Council condemns 'escalatory' Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia The UN Security Council has condemned the "escalatory" attacks by Iran-backed Houthis on Saudi Arabia, including "reckless strikes" on Riyadh's airport. The Saudi capital's international airport has been targeted by strikes 20 times since the beginning of the month, with an attack last weekend killing 13 people and wounding more than 300. In a joint statement shared by the Security Council's president, Greece's Evangelos Sekeris, the 15-member UN body also condemned "continued Houthi attacks and threats against commercial shipping in the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab (Strait)". The statement also "affirmed the inherent right of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia of self-defence in accordance with international law."

items.title: US, Iranian military issue contesting claims over control of Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: US, Iranian military issue contesting claims over control of Strait of Hormuz US Central Command (Centcom) dismissed "Iranian claims" to control the Strait of Hormuz, alleging that the US and its regional partners "control the strait as commercial vessels continue to transit despite unwarranted... aggression" from Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). In a post on X on Thursday, Centcom also denied that the IRGC had killed hundreds of US service members in Jordan and that a Singapore-flagged container ship struck a naval mine in the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday. Meanwhile, Iran's IRIB news reported that Iranian army commander Amir Hatami said the strait is under “full surveillance” by the army and the IRGC, adding that “not a single enemy vessel has been able to enter the maritime space of Oman and the Strait of Hormuz.”

items.title: Gulf states have downplayed damage caused by Iranian strikes: Report
items.summary: Gulf states have downplayed damage caused by Iranian strikes: Report Arabian Gulf monarchies have “suppressed” information about the extent of damage done to their physical infrastructure by attacks from Iran and its allies, Reuters reported on Thursday. Gulf states such as Qatar, the UAE, Bahrain, and Kuwait faced thousands of missile and drone strikes launched by Iran in retaliation for the US-Israeli attack on the Islamic Republic on 28 February. More recently, Saudi Arabia has come under attack from the Houthis in Yemen. The Houthis and Iran targeted civilian infrastructure like pipelines, energy facilities and, in one case, a nuclear energy plant. Reuters' assessment is likely to cast new doubt on how Gulf states describe strikes on their territories. For example, Saudi Arabia’s energy ministry said that a Houthi drone strike caused a "limited fire" at the headquarters of the kingdom's national oil company, Aramco, in Dhahran. But Reuters reported on Wednesday that the headquarters suffered “extensive damage”. Readmore: Gulf states have downplayed damage caused by Iranian strike

items.title: Delegations from over ten countries walk out of Israeli president's CICA summit speech
items.summary: Delegations from over ten countries walk out of Israeli president's CICA summit speech Representatives from more than 10 countries, including Turkey, walked out of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence Building Measures in Asia (CICA) summit in Azerbaijan as Israeli President Isaac Herzog began his speech on Thursday. Iran’s deputy legal affairs minister called for Israel to be expelled from CICA following Herzog's speech in Baku. Kazem Gharibabadi was quoted as saying by Iran's IRIB news that “sustainable security” in Asia was not achieved through “threats and pressure, but through mutual respect, trust-building and equal cooperation among independent states”. “If the international community does not stop America and Israel today, their aggression will spread to all independent countries. The most important source of insecurity and instability in Asia, especially in West Asia, is the Zionist (Israeli) regime; it is time for this regime to be expelled from the CICA mechanism,” he warned.

items.summary: Chinese refiners rush to buy Middle East crude as stocks fall, Kpler says Chinese refiners are stepping up purchases of Middle Eastern crude as record inventory drawdowns and a recovery in refinery activity boost demand for prompt cargoes, according to analytics firm Kpler. Chinese buyers have secured at least 80 million barrels of Saudi crude since mid-September, Kpler said on X. China’s onshore crude inventories fell by about 1.6 million barrels per day in September, the fastest pace on record. Refinery throughput is projected to reach 14.2 million barrels per day by December, adding to pressure on refiners to rebuild stocks. At the same time, Chinese refiners need to replace roughly 1 million barrels per day of Iranian supply, with the US blockade still in place, according to Kpler. Stronger Chinese demand could limit further weakness in Dubai crude pricing, particularly as escalating regional tensions continue to threaten supply flows.

items.title: Pakistan president urges Iran, US to honour Islamabad MoU
items.summary: Pakistan president urges Iran, US to honour Islamabad MoU Pakistani President Asif Ali Zardari has urged the US and Iran to exercise restraint and honour their commitments under the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding. The MoU is a 14-point interim peace agreement signed electronically on 17-18 June between the United States and Iran, with Pakistan acting as the primary mediator. Zardari called for differences to be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy, emphasising the importance of safe maritime navigation through the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea, according to a statement from his office. His remarks came during a meeting with Russian Interior Minister Vladimir Kolokoltsev in Islamabad. Zardari warned that the conflict posed serious challenges to regional stability, global energy security, trade and supply chains, stressing the need to respect the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all states. Kolokoltsev is on a four-day official visit to Pakistan, the first by a Russian interior minister to the South Asian country.

items.title: Attacks on Hormuz shipping at wartime high, report says
items.summary: Attacks on Hormuz shipping at wartime high, report says Iranian missile and drone attacks on ships in and around the Strait of Hormuz were at their most intense in the two weeks to 11 October, the highest level since the US-Israeli strikes began seven months ago, the Financial Times reported. The next most intense period of attacks was during the first two weeks of March, when 13 ships were hit, the newspaper said, citing data from naval agency UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO), which monitors marine security in the region. Shipowners are reconsider carrying cargoes in the region, the report said. Six vessels were attacked on Sunday alone, making it the deadliest day of attacks on shipping near the strait since the start of the conflict, FT calculated. It added that oil shipments through Hormuz fell to just 2.9 million barrels on 11 October, the lowest daily volume this month, according to Kpler.

items.title: Trump says he does not believe China and Russia help Iran, contradicting US intelligence
items.summary: Trump says he does not believe China and Russia help Iran, contradicting US intelligence President Donald Trump said on Monday he did not believe that China and Russia were helping Iran "at all", even as US intelligence reports in recent months have found that both countries directly support Tehran. Trump said on Truth Social that he had seen comments from his critics and opponents that China and Russia were helping Iran. Moscow and Beijing maintain close ties with Tehran. "If they are, it's at a very low level, but I don't believe they are at all. They have too much to lose, and we would know about it, and know about it very fast," Trump wrote. US intelligence assessments from recent months have shown that Russia and China are providing military support to Iran in the form of satellite imagery for targeting purposes and components for weapons, according to two people briefed on the matter.

items.title: 'Major wipeout' of 2006 proportions could force a new GOP reckoning
items.summary: Republicans could be looking at a major wipeout in the midterm elections. Their tiny House majority was always going to be difficult to maintain, but the Senate should not be in play at all. Yet it surely is, with Democrats leading in nearly all the toss-up races , including in the reddest states, and competitive in at least a dozen of the contests that will determine which party controls the upper chamber. The Iran war is a big reason this has come to pass. It has demoralized the least indefatigably partisan part of President Donald Trump’s coalition by abandoning his promise to avoid new forever wars in the Middle East. The conflict has not only distracted from the affordability focus that many voters were expecting when they threw out the Democrats in 2024, but also directly cuts against it by spiking energy prices and increasing inflation overall at a time when it might have otherwise continued to come down. At the time of writing, the missile strike on King Khalid international airport has killed at least 13 people and left 300 injured, marking a significant turn in a regional conflagration that is only getting more intense. It was the single most deadly attack on any Gulf country since the US and Israel launched their war on Iran in February. In Saudi Arabia, a country that is unaccustomed to such fatalities, the death toll is bewilderingly high and likely to prompt a bloody response. Over the past year, the Gulf has entered a new era of instability that is not temporary and cannot be reversed. His sharpest critics see this as ranging from sycophantic revenge on the general officer class to simply misguided personnel policy. items.title: Why Saudi Arabia has returned to war in Yemen
items.summary: This article was republished with permission from the Arab Center Washington DC. When Ansar Allah—commonly referred to as the Houthis— seized Yemen’s Red Sea coastline and strategic islands in the Bab al-Mandab Strait on September 10, 2026, they appeared to gain the upper hand in Yemen’s long-running conflict. However, in early October Saudi-backed government forces began to retake some of the captured territory and Saudi Arabia launched a punishing assault on Houthi positions from the air. France , Pakistan , and the United States have all sent personnel to help the kingdom counter the Houthi offensive. Outside the region, some have portrayed the Houthi offensive as another theater within the broader US-Israeli war on Iran. However, this broader regional war is separate from the war in Yemen, which can be traced back to the Houthi takeover of Yemen’s capital Sanaa in September 2014 and the decision by neighboring Saudi Arabia to launch a coalition to oust them in March 2015. Since the war on Iran began in late February, at least 16 Indian seafarers have been killed.

Wereldleiders spreken schande van de moedwillige aanval op een burgerdoel en noemen het een gevaarlijke escalatie van de strijd op het Arabische schiereiland. Twaalf mensen kwamen om en meer dan 300 raakten gewond toen de passagiersterminal gistermiddag werd geraakt. Het is daarmee de zwaarste aanval op een Saudisch doel sinds de strijd in Jemen halverwege dit jaar weer oplaaide. Eerder deze week werd de luchthaven ook al geraakt door een aanval uit Jemen. Van de aanval zijn maar beperkt beelden beschikbaar omdat Saudi-Arabië een zware censuur kent. Wie beelden van aanvallen of schade deelt, kan een zware straf krijgen. Verschillende ambassades hebben landgenoten daarom afgeraden beelden te plaatsen of door te sturen. Toch kwam er wat beeld van de aanval naar buiten: VN-gezant voor Jemen Hans Grundberg noemt de aanval een ernstige escalatie. items.title: Trump says Iran is ‘failing badly’ as conflict in Yemen widens
items.summary: Trump says Iran is ‘failing badly’ as conflict in Yemen widens US President Donald Trump on Friday left open the possibility of further military action against Iran as fighting intensifies in Yemen and Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia have led to a renewed offensive. Asked why possible US military action against Iran might be delayed until after the 3 November midterm elections rather than carried out immediately, Trump told reporters: “Well, we may. I think we’ll see, but I think that, uh, they’re failing badly. Their country is failing badly." "The military is defeated. They have no navy, they have no air force. Uh, they have 300 percent inflation and, uh, Iran is in very bad shape.” The remarks, recorded in a transcript of Trump’s 9 October press briefing, did not include a specific timeline or details of what action Washington might take. The US and Israel launched their war against Iran on 28 February. Tehran responded with missile and drone attacks across the region, while disruption to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz has threatened global energy supplies. Read more: Trump

items.title: Israeli politician says assassinating Ali Khamenei was a ‘mistake’
items.summary: Israeli politician says assassinating Ali Khamenei was a ‘mistake’ The leader of Israel’s Democrats party on Saturday has called the assassination of Iranian Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei a “mistake”. “I think, unequivocally, the elimination of Khamenei, the father, was a mistake - not because he didn’t deserve to die, only because it doesn’t serve the interests of the State of Israel,” Yair Golan said. He also added that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s goal of toppling the Iranian government was “unrealistic”. Khamenei was assassinated at the beginning of the US-Israel war and has been succeeded by his son, Mojtaba. The new supreme leader is believed to be far less risk-averse than his father, who had issued a fatwa in 2003 banning nuclear weapons in Iran. items.summary: Yousof Azizi: The Iranian-American scholar pressured by the FBI to return to Iran Monday 13 April started as a normal day for Yousof Azizi, a PhD student at Virginia Tech University in America. In the morning, he took his 12-year-old daughter and four-year-old son to their schools in Baltimore, Maryland, before returning home. A vocal opponent of the war on Iran, he had been living in the US for nearly 13 years and was recognised as a prominent political commentator on Persian-language media platforms and on his YouTube channel, which has more than 68,000 subscribers. Azizi had also been involved in discussions with Congress in relation to the Iran nuclear deal during Barack Obama’s presidency. When he arrived back home that April morning, a number of FBI vehicles were parked outside his residence. Upon exiting his car, Azizi found himself surrounded by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents, their rifles pointing straight at him. items.title: Increased vessel attacks drive Hormuz oil exports 'sharply lower', report says
items.summary: Increased vessel attacks drive Hormuz oil exports 'sharply lower', report says Hormuz oil exports were “sharply lower,” falling to a seven-day average of 9.9 million barrels per day as of October 7, 42 percent below prewar levels and down from about 15.5 million in September, according to Kpler data cited by the Financial Times. Kpler said that flows had recovered to prewar levels in September but "intensified attacks on vessels" had driven exports "sharply lower" this week. Energy analyst Rory Johnston also said that the latest estimate puts Hormuz seven-day average oil flow peaking at 16.2 mbpd on September 24. "Then Iran really picked up its shipping attacks and that flow unsurprisingly pulled back by 3-4 mbpd," he wrote on X. "Now seeing flow at 12-13 mbpd over the past two weeks."

"President Trump zal nooit toestaan dat het Internationaal Strafhof Amerikanen vervolgt", zegt minister Rubio van Buitenlandse Zaken in een videoboodschap op X . "Daarom legt de VS vandaag sancties op aan het Internationaal Strafhof. We zullen transacties met dit schurkachtige hof verbieden, hen afsnijden van middelen en hun vermogen om te functioneren lamleggen." Eerder legde de Amerikaanse regering sancties op aan individuele aanklagers en rechters. Nu breidt de VS het pakket maatregelen uit. "We hebben het Strafhof niet nodig", zegt Rubio. "Amerikanen vallen niet onder de jurisdictie van dit 'nep-ICC'."
